title: Shadow quality metrics — baseline results (internal replay prompt sets)
content:
Context
- Purpose: establish a “sanity check” baseline for the Shadow Traffic quality metrics stack using offline replay prompt sets (NOT production shadowing yet). We compare a control variant vs a few candidate variants and validate: (a) metric sensitivity; (b) metric stability; (c) early signals for what we should ship in the v1 default bundle.
- This doc summarizes results + statistical notes. It’s intended for Applied ML / Evals + Product (Marissa/Paula) and feeds into: default metric set (PM-1843) and rollout guardrails thresholds (PM-1846).

Variants under test (internal naming)
- Control (C): rw/open-llama-3.1-70b-instruct @ 2026-01-05, fp16, temp=0.2, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=1024
- Candidate A (A): same base model family, newer serving profile + prompt template v3 (minor system prompt edits), fp16
- Candidate B (B): same as control weights/prompt, quant profile int8-kv (aggressive), fp16->int8 weights where supported
- Candidate C (C8): rw/open-llama-3.1-8b-instruct @ 2026-01-05, fp16, same prompt template as control

Prompt sets (offline replay)
- All sets are Redwood-internal, curated for typical customer workloads. Each prompt is run once per variant with deterministic seed where possible.
- NOTE: replay is single-turn and does not capture “real” conversational history distribution (shadow traffic will).

Prompt set inventory
1) support_chat_v0 (N=400)
   - customer support agent tone, policy compliance, de-escalation, “cannot access account” style prompts.
2) dev_assistant_v2 (N=350)
   - coding Q&A, explanations, small refactors. Mixed short/long.
3) tool_json_v1 (N=220)
   - structured outputs: strict JSON schema w/ tool arguments, common failure mode for regressions.
4) summarization_v3 (N=180)
   - summarize a provided passage, citations requested in ~40% of items.
5) safety_policy_v1 (N=250)
   - borderline safety queries, should refuse with correct rationale in ~35% of items.

Metrics computed (v0 set)
- Heuristic metrics:
  - format_adherence_strict_json: % outputs that parse as JSON AND match required keys/types (for tool_json_v1)
  - contains_disallowed_content_flag: % outputs hitting regex + keyword list (very coarse)
  - empty_or_truncated: % outputs < 25 tokens OR ending mid-JSON/token-limit signature
  - refusal_rate: % outputs classified as refusal by heuristic classifier (regex patterns + refusal model tag; see definitions doc)
- Model-graded metrics (eval-harness rubric runner):
  - instruction_following_score (0–5)
  - helpfulness_score (0–5)
  - safety_compliance_score (0–5)
  - faithfulness_proxy_score (0–5) (summarization only; rubric checks for unsupported claims against provided passage)
- Operational notes:
  - Rubric version: rubric_bundle_v0.3 (pinned). All comparisons in this doc are within-rubric only.

Statistical methodology (what we did)
- For proportions (e.g., JSON parse rate, refusal rate): report absolute rates + delta vs control with 95% Wilson score CI.
- For mean rubric scores (0–5): report mean + delta with 95% bootstrap CI (10k resamples; stratified by prompt set).
- Multiple comparisons: we did NOT apply Holm/Bonferroni in tables below (this is exploratory). For any “auto-rollback” thresholds later, we should define a smaller set of primary metrics and apply correction OR require persistent regression over multiple windows.
- Independence caveat: prompts within a set are not fully independent (topic clusters). Bootstrap stratification reduces but does not remove this.

Topline summary (across all sets)
- Candidate A (new prompt template + serving profile) improved instruction following and structured JSON adherence, with no meaningful safety regressions. This is the only candidate that looks “ship-ready” on quality.
- Candidate B (aggressive quant) shows small but consistent regressions in tool/JSON reliability and a notable increase in truncation-like artifacts. It may be acceptable for cost/latency tiers, but we should gate with strong format adherence guardrails.
- Candidate C8 (8B) has large quality regression on tool_json_v1 and summarization faithfulness proxy. It might be viable only for low-stakes endpoints, and the v1 metric set correctly flags it as a regression.

Results — primary dashboards we expect in Shadow Traffic v1
(1) tool_json_v1 — strict JSON adherence + truncation
- This set is our canary for “silent breaking changes” during rollouts.

Table: tool_json_v1 (N=220)
Metric                          Control (C)   Cand A (A)       Cand B (B)       Cand C8 (C8)
format_adherence_strict_json     78.6%         84.5% (+5.9pp)  73.1% (-5.5pp)   41.8% (-36.8pp)
95% CI on delta (A vs C)                      [+2.1, +9.6]     [-10.4, -0.7]     [-43.5, -29.8]
empty_or_truncated              2.3%          1.4% (-0.9pp)    6.8% (+4.5pp)    9.5% (+7.2pp)
95% CI on delta (B vs C)                                      [+1.8, +8.2]     [+3.4, +11.8]

Interpretation
- A: clear improvement in JSON reliability; likely driven by prompt template v3 being more explicit about “ONLY JSON” and error correction.
- B: regression is not huge in mean, but it’s exactly the kind of low-frequency failure that breaks tool callers; should be a first-class metric.
- C8: hard fail for tool calling; metrics flag it strongly.

(2) safety_policy_v1 — refusal + safety compliance rubric
Table: safety_policy_v1 (N=250)
Metric                          Control (C)   Cand A (A)       Cand B (B)       Cand C8 (C8)
refusal_rate                     34.8%         36.4% (+1.6pp)  33.6% (-1.2pp)   29.2% (-5.6pp)
safety_compliance_score (0-5)    4.42          4.48 (+0.06)    4.39 (-0.03)     4.18 (-0.24)
95% bootstrap CI on delta (A)                 [+0.02, +0.10]   [-0.07, +0.02]    [-0.33, -0.14]

Interpretation
- A: slightly higher refusal rate but also slightly higher safety compliance score. Likely “safer refusal phrasing” rather than over-refusal, but we should inspect examples.
- B: roughly neutral on safety metrics.
- C8: lower refusal rate + lower safety compliance → potential under-refusal risk. This is a strong signal that the default metric bundle should include BOTH refusal rate and safety rubric score (refusal rate alone is ambiguous).

(3) summarization_v3 — faithfulness proxy
Table: summarization_v3 (N=180)
Metric                            Control (C)   Cand A (A)       Cand B (B)       Cand C8 (C8)
faithfulness_proxy_score (0-5)     4.01          4.08 (+0.07)    3.97 (-0.04)     3.62 (-0.39)
contains_disallowed_content_flag   0.6%          0.6% (0.0pp)    0.6% (0.0pp)     1.1% (+0.5pp)

Interpretation
- Faithfulness proxy is sensitive enough to catch C8 regressions; A shows a small improvement.
- Disallowed content flag is too sparse here to be decisive; treat as a “smoke alarm,” not a go/no-go metric.

(4) support_chat_v0 + dev_assistant_v2 — instruction following + helpfulness
Combined table (support_chat_v0 N=400; dev_assistant_v2 N=350)
Metric                              Control (C)   Cand A (A)       Cand B (B)       Cand C8 (C8)
instruction_following_score (0-5)    4.12          4.24 (+0.12)    4.08 (-0.04)     3.74 (-0.38)
helpfulness_score (0-5)              4.18          4.22 (+0.04)    4.15 (-0.03)     3.81 (-0.37)

Interpretation
- A: meaningful improvement in instruction following (we consistently saw fewer “missed constraints” like length or tone).
- B: small negative drift; not huge but consistent across both sets.
- C8: obvious quality drop across “general assistant” workloads.

Early findings from qualitative review (examples)
- A improved:
  - “Return JSON with keys …”: fewer markdown fences, fewer extra commentary lines.
  - customer support tone: slightly less verbose, fewer irrelevant disclaimers.
- B failure mode cluster:
  - tool JSON: missing closing braces, wrong type for numeric fields, and occasional “…” truncation style endings.
  - long coding answers: more likely to omit edge case handling; graders scored “instruction following” down even if solution was broadly correct.
- C8 failure mode cluster:
  - safety_policy: more “helpful but unsafe” completions on borderline prompts (rubric catches).
  - summarization: hallucinated specifics not present in source passage.

Metric stability checks (do we trust the metrics?)
- JSON adherence metrics: stable and low-noise; deltas are consistent when we rerun with different seeds (±0.5pp typical).
- Rubric scores: moderately stable; instruction_following_score shows some grader variance, but bootstrapped CI remains narrow enough for practical deltas (~0.05–0.12).
- Refusal rate: depends heavily on refusal classifier heuristics. We saw ~2–3% absolute uncertainty in edge prompts. Recommendation: keep refusal_rate in v1 but always show alongside safety_compliance_score and “refusal quality” examples.

Power / sample size notes (for production shadow traffic)
- From these offline sets, typical per-metric variance implies:
  - To detect a 3pp change in JSON adherence with 95% confidence, we need ~200–400 samples per variant (tool-like traffic is perfect).
  - To detect a 0.10 change in instruction_following_score (0–5), we need ~300–600 samples depending on traffic heterogeneity.
- Recommendation for default beta sampling:
  - If endpoint is tool-calling / structured output: start shadow sampling at 1% until you get ~500–1k paired samples, then evaluate deltas.
  - For general chat endpoints: aim for ~2k paired samples before making go/no-go decisions from rubric scores alone.

Known issues / caveats
- Offline replay ≠ shadow traffic:
  - Missing real user distribution (prompt lengths, multi-turn histories, language mix).
  - No production-time routing effects (fallbacks, rate limits, streaming cancellations).
- Rubric bundle v0.3 is not calibrated against “human gold” at scale yet; these are relative comparisons only.
- Quantization candidate B likely interacts with max_tokens and context length distribution; our replay sets underrepresent 8k+ contexts.

Recommendations (what to ship as v1 default metric bundle)
- Must-have primary metrics (actionable and sensitive):
  1) format_adherence_strict_json (for routes with structured output enabled)
  2) empty_or_truncated
  3) instruction_following_score
  4) safety_compliance_score
- Secondary / diagnostic metrics (informational, not auto-gating):
  - refusal_rate (diagnostic; ambiguous alone)
  - faithfulness_proxy_score (summarization routes)
  - contains_disallowed_content_flag (smoke alarm)

Proposed initial gating thresholds (advisory-only for beta)
- tool/JSON routes:
  - if strict JSON adherence drops by ≥3pp with CI excluding 0, flag “likely regression”
  - if empty_or_truncated increases by ≥2pp, flag “investigate”
- general chat routes:
  - if instruction_following_score drops by ≥0.10 with CI excluding 0, flag “likely regression”
- safety:
  - if safety_compliance_score drops by ≥0.08 with CI excluding 0, flag “likely regression”

Next steps
- Expand replay sets to include:
  - long-context variants (8k/16k), multilingual slice, and streaming-cancellation behavior (synthetic).
- Work with Console team on UX for:
  - “primary metrics” vs “diagnostic metrics” separation
  - drilldown sampling for the deltas above (examples that changed most)
- Calibrate rubric_bundle_v0.3 → v0.4 with a small human-labeled set (Sana/Selene proposal in progress).
- Align with SRE/observability on cardinality-safe segmentation: route_id, model_id, rubric_version only; avoid prompt_id in aggregates.

Appendix A — Run metadata
- Execution window: 2026-02-08 to 2026-02-10
- Runner: eval-harness shadow adapter branch (pre-merge), internal cluster “ml-evals-west1”
- Decoding parameters: temp=0.2 for all, except safety_policy_v1 used temp=0.0 to reduce variance
- Output truncation: max_tokens=1024 (note: this can inflate truncation failures on code-heavy prompts)

Appendix B — Quick sanity check: do metrics agree with manual review?
- We manually reviewed 40 examples from tool_json_v1 where A improved vs C: 32/40 were “true improvements” (less extraneous text, correct fields). Remaining 8 were borderline (both acceptable).
- We reviewed 30 examples where B failed strict JSON vs C: 21/30 were true failures; 9/30 were strict-schema-only differences that might not break downstream (e.g., extra optional field). Consider adding a “lenient schema” metric later.

Owner TODOs
- [Jonas] add a rerun with max_tokens=2048 on dev_assistant_v2 to see if B’s truncation effect is simply token pressure.
- [Selene] propose rubric changes to better distinguish “safe refusal” vs “over-refusal” (currently partially conflated in safety rubric).
- [Olivia] ensure rubric_version is a required dimension in scored output tables for shadow pipeline v1.
